data.title: PR 21: semantic neighbor generation around the causal core (RFC 0032 strategies, envelope-checked, deterministic)

data.body:
[HIGH][CWE-754] Unsupported and unrun neighbors can produce Complete receipt coverage. `dispose` records `Realized::Unsupported` only in a counter (lines 1648-1656). The final verdict ignores unsupported and `NotRun` outcomes (lines 1966-1979). `receipt_coverage` then omits every `NotRun` strategy and serializes only executed neighbors as explored (lines 1266-1309). The committed register evidence demonstrates the failure: `pr21_impl01_neighborhood.evidence.txt:43-47` has 16 valid message neighbors, 8 unsupported neighbors, and two unrun strategies, yet reports `Complete`; its receipt projection at line 179 hides those gaps. RFC 0032:145 requires neighboring schedules, faults, and values to be explored. RFC 0032:178 requires unsupported semantics to remain distinct and inconclusive. A promotion-gate consumer can therefore receive schema-valid coverage that silently excludes selected fault semantics.

Failure modes: A selected strategy can be unavailable or partly unsupported while the campaign reports `Complete`; the projection then presents only the supported subset as coverage.
Edge cases: An empty selected set, every selected strategy returning `NotRun`, every valid candidate returning `Unsupported`, and the committed mixed 8-of-16 message case all reach this path.
Rollback: Keep receipt projection and gate-5 wiring unavailable. Refuse projection, or return typed `UnsupportedSemanticFeature`, whenever a selected strategy is unrun or any valid neighbor is unsupported. Define the required strategy profile explicitly.
Monitoring: Compare selected, ran, valid, executed, unsupported, and unrealizable counts. Alert on `Complete` with selected greater than ran, unsupported greater than zero, or no executed neighbors.
Validation: Add negative tests for empty selection, all `NotRun`, all unsupported, and mixed supported/unsupported campaigns. Each must refuse receipt projection and preserve a typed unsupported outcome.
Counterevidence: The crate-local record preserves unsupported and unrun counts, and production gate wiring is not present. The exported receipt projection discards that evidence.

[MEDIUM][CWE-670] Budget exhaustion uses the wrong terminal state and provides no continuation. RFC 0032:178-180 requires gate 5 to remain `pending` and return `BudgetExhausted` with a continuation. RFC 0032:226-227 repeats that a truncated campaign needs a continuation. This path instead returns `Verdict::Inconclusive(ResourceExhausted)` (lines 1966-1975). `receipt_coverage` explicitly permits that verdict (lines 1283-1288). The frontier is only a string, and this module exposes no continuation or resume API. The unit test at `crates/continuum-repair/tests/pr21_neighborhood.rs:343-389` locks in the conflicting verdict and proves only that a fresh rerun shares a prefix. The integration test at `crates/continuum-asupersync/tests/pr21_impl01_neighborhood.rs:1687-1718` also projects the truncated result.

Failure modes: Callers cannot resume a committed campaign monotonically. They can treat a resumable pending campaign as terminal inconclusive or project its partial coverage.
Edge cases: Zero run or work budget, exhaustion during candidate charging, exhaustion during a random walk, and exhaustion before later strategies all lack resumable state.
Rollback: Keep budgeted campaign and receipt wiring unavailable. Return a typed `BudgetExhausted` result with an opaque continuation. Do not map exhaustion to `Verdict::Inconclusive` or permit promotion coverage projection.
Monitoring: Count budget suspensions, emitted continuations, resume attempts, and monotonic frontier advances. Reject any resource-exhausted campaign that lacks exactly one continuation.
Validation: Sweep every budget boundary, serialize and restore each continuation, resume to a byte-identical full result, and prove gate 5 remains pending until completion.
Counterevidence: Deterministic fresh reruns reproduce the same prefix and the record discloses truncation. A rerun prefix is not a continuation and does not preserve committed progress.

data.reason: BLOCK: one HIGH fail-open coverage projection and one MEDIUM budget-continuation contract violation remain unresolved.
